report:
Finding: Model B looks instruction-tuned (chat/assistant-like) with a strong coding/algorithmic bias, while Model A appears more base-like.

Why I think this:
- Patchscope readouts consistently turn an identity prompt into assistant-style responses: “This is a valid question.”, “This is a good start…”, step-by-step guidance, and multiple Python snippets (is_prime, solve, code fences ```python). There are also explicit echo/identity-transform patterns (“cat -> cat”, “1135 -> 1135”), which are common in instruction/SFT data.
- The residual difference is heavily concentrated at the first token (p0) across many layers, peaking late (layer 25), consistent with an assistant preamble/style kick-in right at the start of generation.
- Logit-lens hints at expository/instructional vocabulary (e.g., “recommendations”, “refused”, “optimize”, “proactive”, “worst”, “blitz”, “adhere”), and headline-like tokens (“headlines”, “Driver”, “Names”), which together fit a more curated, instruction/explanation/news-summarization flavor than raw web text.

Bottom line: The evidence supports a behavioral/objective shift toward instruction-following with code-oriented examples and echo/identity tasks (B minus A).
